title: Data Center Controls Tech, Controls Team
descriptionHtml:
The Data Center Global Controls team is looking for exceptional individuals to join our Controls organization as a Controls Technician for Service & Construction of the Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring System (EPMS) within Amazon data centers. If you are passionate about the Customer Experience, think and act globally and have the ability to contribute to major new innovations in the area of building controls and automation this is the challenge you are looking for! The candidate will possess technical background and experience in installation, troubleshooting, operations and/or maintenance of field sensors, controllers, wiring, networking and programming associated with the industrial controls systems. The candidate may also have relevant experience operating and maintaining mission critical electrical and mechanical systems. A Controls Technician shall be responsible for participating in the installation, testing, troubleshooting and startup of equipment and controls system associated with the BMS and EPMS system deployment in the data centers. A Controls Technician is expected to actively innovate on behalf of their customers in the area of Data Center building automation.

Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.

Key job responsibilities
• Primarily work in and support multiple data centers by deploying, servicing, and upgrading BMS and EPMS systems.
• Mentor and train Facilities team members on the operation and control of BMS and EPMS systems.
• Manage small to medium-sized projects and programs.
• Perform point-to-point checkouts between field devices and controllers.
• Perform first-line diagnostics, troubleshooting, and maintenance of programming code and hardware associated with BMS and EPMS in data centers.
• Execute provisioning processes for servers, controllers, industrial PCs, and network configurations, including communication testing between third-party devices and controllers or servers.
• Install, replace, configure, and calibrate sensors.
• Read and interpret electrical schematics and control panel drawings with a basic understanding of closed-loop controls, field sensor scaling, and functions typically performed by industrial controllers.
• Supervise low-voltage electrical contractors performing wiring and installation of field devices in compliance with AWS requirements.
• Provide commissioning and systems-level testing support.
• Create red-lined drawings and documentation of systems.
• Follow change management processes to generate work requests and methods of procedures.
• Participate in factory witness tests at vendor or panel builder facilities.
• Perform root cause analysis during testing and commissioning.
• Ensure personnel on site utilize proper safety methodology.
• Perform service activities including monitoring and reviewing ticketing systems, conducting root cause analysis, and prioritizing tasks.
• Actively manage service agreements including vendor labor scheduling, quality assurance, and financial invoice review.
• Participate in material handling tasks such as lifting, carrying, or moving up to 50 lbs of equipment, and utilize OSHA-standard safety equipment including limited weight-bearing work platforms, ladders, step stools, and personal protective equipment (PPE) such as safety harnesses.
• Perform other tasks as assigned by manager


Physical Requirements:
· Walk job-sites in uneven terrain and work at heights and from ladders.
· Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch
or crawl.
· On occasions, lift and/or move up to 49 pounds; and participate in group lifts for 50 pounds or more.

A day in the life
A typical day is attending morning construction/commissioning meetings, assessing and prioritization of project tasks and service tickets for the given day. Field work which requires configuring controllers, testing sensors, troubleshooting, safety site walks, and supporting general startup processes. Technician is responsible for logging their daily efforts in construction and service related AWS tools.

The mission of the Data Center Controls Engineering team is to manage the design, deployment, and service of a highly reliable electrical and mechanical control system for the life-cycle of an AWS data center.

About the team
As a member of the Global Controls Team, you will collaborate with highly motivated operators, engineers and technicians in the data center industry to maintain and optimize critical infrastructure systems. You will be responsible for troubleshooting and maintaining the Building Management System (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring System (EPMS) while developing new processes and standards that drive innovation in the controls space.
AWS data centers utilize sophisticated industrial control systems to automatically operate mechanical equipment, maintaining optimal temperature and pressure conditions throughout the facilities. These systems integrate and monitor multiple critical components, including generators, uninterruptible power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic and static transfer switches, air-cooled and water-cooled chillers, pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, Computer Room Air Handlers (CRAHs), and air economizers. Within this industrial control system infrastructure, the BMS serves as the primary control platform for all mechanical systems within the data center, while the EPMS functions as the primary monitoring platform for all electrical systems. This position offers the opportunity to work with cutting-edge technology in mission-critical environments while contributing to the reliability and efficiency of AWS's global infrastructure.

Basic qualifications

- High school or equivalent diploma
- Basic understanding of Industrial controls system, knowledge of meters, devices, sensors, relays and troubleshooting utilizing standard hand tools, digital metering, or calibration/diagnostic equipment in a data center, hospitals, large commercial complex, water, power, oil & gas or similar industries
- 1+ years of experience working with low voltage controls, wiring, networking signals, electrical and mechanical systems, computers and operating systems
- Ability to work non-standard hours and differing work rotations/shifts and overtime as required.

Preferred qualifications

- High School or equivalent diploma
- International Society of Automation (ISA) Certified Controls System Technician (CCST) Level I or higher certification.
- Experiencing using common communication protocols (MQTT, BACnet, and/or MODBUS).
- 5+ years of experience in controls/automation, construction or related field in a technical environment
- Demonstrated understanding of engineering documentation, electrical and mechanical diagrams, and standard operating procedures.
- Experience in data centers or mission critical environment
- Fundamental knowledge of network design and layout as well as low voltage (copper/ fiber) cabling.
- Prior AWS/Amazon experience
- 4+ Yr. Military Service

title: Mechatronic Apprentice I
descriptionHtml:
Operations is at the heart of Amazon’s business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. Reliability Maintenance & Engineering (RME) are the business partners that work tirelessly behind the scenes to make it all happen. We drive continuous improvement, and maintain all of the Robotics and Material Handling Equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey!
About the Role:

As a Mechatronics & Robotics Apprentice (MRA), you will learn to combine electronic, mechanical, computer and automation engineering skills at the workplace. During on-the-job learning (OJL) you will work with complex high-performance manufacturing systems and will learn to analyze, troubleshoot, and repair systems to maintain process efficiency. The focus of your role will be to learn the skills and abilities to ensure safety regulations and policies are adhered to, assist in the installation, maintenance, and repair of the automated packaging and distribution equipment, ensure preventative maintenance is conducted on time to a high standard, and provide high levels of equipment availability through continuous improvement.

You will be paired with journey workers to carry out their work at various facilities, including high automation and robotics facilities in connection with service operations. You will be expected to complete work based on technical documents and instructions and carry out your work in compliance with the relevant provisions and safety regulations.

You should be an effective communicator, work well in a team, and be self-motivated. You must have the ability to work collaboratively and coordinate your activities with upstream and downstream operations partners. In addition to developing your skills, you will be mentored by senior technicians to grow in your role.


Key job responsibilities
Key job responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
• You will perform preventative/predictive maintenance of conveyance equipment using the appropriate job plans, procedures, and manuals.

• You will conduct maintenance and basic troubleshooting of robotics and robotic work cells.

• You will troubleshoot electrical and mechanical problems related to all material handling equipment components.

• You will maintain and troubleshoot motors, photo eyes, relays, proximity sensors, solenoids, motor starters, tachs, etc.
• You must be able to move up to 49lbs, stand and walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, climb ladders and gangways safely, and without limitation, as well as perform regular bending, lifting, stretching, and reaching both below the waist and above the head

Program Requirements:

- Experience troubleshooting and repairing operational items
- Knowledge of mathematics
- Experience measurement reading and interpretation
- Work flexible schedules including weekends, nights, and holidays

Preferred qualifications

- 4+ years of military experience
- Experience conducting predictive and preventative maintenance procedures
- Experience troubleshooting and diagnosing material handling equipment (MHE)
- Experience implementing safety standards
- Experience reading blueprints and electrical schematics

title: System Development Engineer, Astra ADC
descriptionHtml:
This is an excellent opportunity to join Amazon's world-class technical team at HQ2 in Arlington, VA, working with some of the best and brightest engineers while developing your skills and furthering your career within one of the most innovative technology companies anywhere.

Amazon Software Builder Experience (ASBX) Astra ADC provides the foundational services that every Amazon builder depends on to develop, deploy, and operate software from continuous deployment orchestration to testing infrastructure and configuration management. Our team owns and operates critical ASBX services across Amazon's most secure and isolated environments, including Apollo (deployment), Pipelines (continuous delivery), Test on Demand/Hydra (integration testing), AppConfig (feature management), Multi-Region (resource replication), Builder MCP, and AIM (AI agent infrastructure). We ensure these services maintain parity, reliability, and security across all partitions.

A successful Engineer joining the team will do much more than write code and triage problems. They will operate services at scale in air-gapped environments where standard commercial tooling doesn't exist, drive cross-partition deployment parity, and build the automation that keeps Amazon's most sensitive workloads shipping safely. They will dive deep into complex distributed systems issues and work diligently to improve the builder experience.

The ideal candidate will:

- Be great fun to work with. Our company credo is "Work hard. Have fun. Make history." The right candidate will love what they do and instinctively know how to make work fun.
- Have strong Linux & Networking Fundamentals. The ideal candidate will have deep experience working with Linux, preferably in large-scale, distributed environments. You understand networking technology, how services communicate across isolated boundaries, and regularly take part in deep-dive troubleshooting and technical post-mortem discussions to identify root causes of complex issues.
- Love to code. Whether it's building deployment automation, creating AI-powered operational tooling, or solving complex cross-partition orchestration problems, the ideal candidate will love using technology to solve problems. You have a solid understanding of software development methodology and CI/CD practices.
- Think Big. The ideal candidate will build and deploy solutions that enable thousands of Amazon builders to ship software reliably across multiple isolated regions. You will strive to improve and streamline processes to allow delivery at massive scale.
This position requires that the candidate selected must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance. The position further requires that, after start, the selected candidate obtain and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph or commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.


A day in the life
You start the morning reviewing deployment health across isolated regions, checking alarms and on-call handoffs. Mid-morning, you're deep in a code review for a cross-partition automation fix, then jump into a design discussion on how to bring a new ASBX service capability to air-gapped environments. After lunch, you troubleshoot a deployment pipeline issue, tracing it from orchestration logs to a configuration mismatch, and ship the fix before end of day. Between the technical depth and the autonomy to own problems end-to-end, no two days look the same.

About the team
Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS)
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree, or CSSLP (Certified Secure Software Lifecycle Professional)
- 2+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 1+ years of designing or architecting (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 4+ years of administrative experience in networking, storage systems, operating systems and hands-on systems engineering experience
- Knowledge of systems engineering fundamentals (networking, storage, operating systems)
- Experience programming with at least one modern language such as C++, C#, Java, Python, Golang, PowerShell, Ruby

title: Arquiteto(a) de Soluções, Brazil Solutions Architecture, Enterprise Cross Industry
descriptionHtml:
Você está em busca de uma carreira com grandes desafios? Possui curiosidade e persistência? Você quer se desenvolver em um ambiente inovador, onde experimentamos coisas novas e sonhamos grande? Quer fazer parte do futuro da computação em nuvem com uma equipe obcecada por ajudar os clientes?

Se sim, junte-se à nossa equipe AWS no Brasil como Arquiteto(a) de Soluções e ajude nossos clientes a mudarem o mundo! A AWS é a plataforma de nuvem mais adotada e mais abrangente do mundo, suportando milhões de clientes, incluindo startups, grandes empresas e órgãos governamentais.

Nesta função, sua criatividade conectará tecnologia a soluções tangíveis. Você trabalhará todos os dias para ajudar clientes a aproveitarem ao máximo os serviços da AWS, para que possam inovar, prosperar e transformar nosso país. Você terá a oportunidade de aprender novas habilidades e aprimorar as suas existentes. Você criará e compartilhará conteúdo técnico, arquiteturas de referência e práticas recomendadas. Você divulgará e educará sobre a tecnologia da AWS.

Esperamos de você motivação, trabalho em colaboração com pessoas ao redor do mundo, disposição para enfrentar desafios, paixão pelo que faz e se divertir ao fazê-lo. Você deve gostar de treinar, desenhar e criar soluções em nuvem para um conjunto diversificado e desafiador de clientes.

Key job responsibilities
As equipes de Arquitetura de Soluções possuem 4 responsabilidades principais:

1. Atuar de forma consultiva para clientes. Em parceria com a equipe de contas, formular e executar uma estratégia para viabilizar o sucesso do cliente. Ajudar clientes a adotar os serviços da AWS e fazer o melhor uso deles, gerando receita como resultado. Educar clientes sobre a proposta de valor da AWS e participar de discussões de arquitetura para garantir que as soluções sejam desenhadas para uma implantação bem-sucedida na nuvem. Criar confiança com equipes técnicas dentro de clientes para que sejam cloud advocates.
2. Ser referência técnica. Transferir conhecimento para clientes. Capturar e compartilhar conhecimento e boas práticas na comunidade de arquitetura de soluções da AWS. Contribuir com publicações para o cliente da AWS, como whitepapers, postagens ou blogs. Apresentar e contribuir em workshops, grupos de usuários, vídeos online e conferências.
3. Estar em crescimento profissional contínuo. Manter a curiosidade e o aprendizado. Demonstrar seu aprendizado através das Certificações da AWS. Trabalhar com outras pessoas para ajudá-las a entregar mais. Participar de encontros e conferências.
4. Desenvolver e executar melhorias organizacionais. Atuar como um elo técnico entre clientes e equipes de engenharia de serviços para melhorar os serviços e recursos da AWS. Contribuir com suas ideias para inovação para times internos e clientes. Simplificar processos que podem ser simplificados. Ajudar a contratar e desenvolver talentos.

About the team
A Amazon Web Services Brasil valoriza a Diversidade, Equidade e Inclusão (DE&I) em todas as nossas posições de trabalho, e por isso atuamos com intencionalidade para que nosso ambiente interno reflita a pluralidade dos mercados em que atuamos e clientes que atendemos.

Aqui na AWS, abraçamos nossas diferenças. Estamos comprometidos em promover nossa cultura de inclusão. Temos 13 employee led groups globalmente, que reúnem os funcionários da Amazon entre organizações e países ao redor do mundo. No Brasil, alguns exemplos incluem o Women@Amazon, o Glamazon (LGBTQIA+) e o Black Employee Network (BEN). A cultura de inclusão da Amazon é reforçada em nossos 16 Princípios de Liderança, que lembram as pessoas a buscar perspectivas diversas, aprender, ter curiosidade e ganhar confiança.

Se você quiser solicitar uma acomodação para a entrevista ou o processo de integração, avise seu recrutador(a) e ele(a) o conectará à nossa equipe de acomodação.

Mentoria e Crescimento profissional
Nossa equipe é dedicada a apoiar as pessoas recém contratadas. Temos uma equipe com ampla variedade de níveis de experiência e cargos, e estamos construindo um ambiente que celebra o compartilhamento de conhecimento e a mentoria. Nós nos preocupamos com o crescimento de sua carreira e nos esforçamos para atribuir projetos que contribuam para que cada pessoa da equipe se desenvolva e possa liderar iniciativas mais complexas no futuro.

A AWS valoriza experiências diversas. Mesmo que você não atenda a todas as qualificações e habilidades preferidas listadas na descrição da vaga, incentivamos os candidatos a se candidatarem. Se sua carreira está apenas começando, não seguiu um caminho tradicional ou inclui experiências alternativas, não deixe que isso o impeça de se candidatar.

Por que AWS?
A Amazon Web Services (AWS) é a plataforma de nuvem mais abrangente e amplamente adotada do mundo. Fomos pioneiros na computação em nuvem e nunca paramos de inovar — é por isso que clientes, desde as startups mais bem-sucedidas até empresas da Global 500, confiam em nosso robusto conjunto de produtos e serviços para impulsionar seus negócios.

Cultura de Equipe Inclusiva
Aqui na AWS, está em nossa natureza aprender e ser curioso. Nossos grupos de afinidade liderados por funcionários promovem uma cultura de inclusão que nos capacita a ter orgulho de nossas diferenças. Eventos contínuos e experiências de aprendizado, incluindo nossas Conversas sobre Raça e Etnia (CORE) e conferências sobre diversidade, nos inspiram a nunca parar de abraçar nossa singularidade.

Mentoria e Crescimento Profissional
Estamos continuamente elevando nosso padrão de desempenho enquanto nos esforçamos para nos tornar o Melhor Empregador da Terra. É por isso que você encontrará aqui compartilhamento infinito de conhecimento, mentoria e outros recursos para desenvolvimento de carreira para ajudá-lo a se desenvolver como um profissional mais completo.

Equilíbrio entre Trabalho e Vida Pessoal
Valorizamos a harmonia entre trabalho e vida pessoal. Alcançar sucesso no trabalho nunca deve vir à custa de sacrifícios em casa, por isso buscamos flexibilidade como parte de nossa cultura de trabalho. Quando nos sentimos apoiados no local de trabalho e em casa, não há nada que não possamos alcançar na nuvem.

- Experiência em design, implementação ou consultoria em aplicações e infraestruturas
- Experiência em desenvolvimento de TI ou implementação/consultoria nas indústrias de software ou internet

Preferred qualifications

- Experiência em desenvolvimento de software ou em setores relacionados à internet

He or she will have responsibility for ensuring all inventory systems and processes are meeting the needs of the business and implementing controls around these processes. Key areas of focus include driving improvement in inventory availability, increasing inventory efficiency and improving product sourcing decisions. The Instock specialist will also drive supply chain program adoption and new programs.

A successful candidate possesses superb business judgment, instock or operations management experience, strong skills in working cross functionally, and a track record of delivering results through others. He or she will excel in having strong analytical capabilities, including experience generating and managing forecasts, reports, and analyses. The position requires an individual who can work autonomously in a demanding and often ambiguous environment, with strong attention to detail and effective prioritization.

Key job responsibilities
1. Define and own the annual instock strategic and operational plan for the category, including availability targets (SoROOS), cost-to-serve goals, inventory turns, and inventory health metrics
2. Lead CPFR (Collaborative Planning, Forecasting, and Replenishment) strategy at the category level — owning monthly, quarterly, and yearly forecast alignment across the vendor portfolio and ensuring buying input parameters are optimized across all accounts
3. Audit and optimize complex forecasting, IPC, and Supply Chain systems to ensure performance within goal/control limits; create long-term category solutions that automate or simplify replenishment and ordering processes

title: Senior Product Manager Tech, PV Partner Experience
descriptionHtml:
Prime Video is a first-stop entertainment destination offering customers a vast collection of premium programming in one app available across thousands of devices. Prime members can customize their viewing experience and find their favorite movies, series, documentaries, and live sports – including Amazon MGM Studios-produced series and movies; licensed fan favorites; and programming from Prime Video add-on subscriptions such as Apple TV+, Max, Crunchyroll and MGM+. All customers, regardless of whether they have Prime membership or not, can rent or buy titles via the Prime Video Store, and can enjoy even more content for free with ads.

Are you interested in shaping the future of entertainment? Do you want to invent, disrupt and redefine what entertainment means for fans, creators, and communities all around the globe?

As part of the Prime Video team, you’ll get to work on projects that are fast-paced, challenging, and varied. Also, you’ll get to experiment with new possibilities, take risks, and collaborate with remarkable people.

We’ll look for you to bring your diverse perspectives, ideas, and skill sets to make Prime Video even better for our customers. With global opportunities for talented creatives, technologists, marketing professionals and so much more, you can decide where a career with Prime Video takes you!

Prime Video's Partner Experience team builds the platform that 10,000+ content partners depend on to deliver, promote, measure, and grow on Prime Video. We're looking for a Technical Sr. Product Manager to identify and own our highest-leverage partner-facing product opportunities, from zero to one.

This is a high-autonomy role for someone who thrives in ambiguity. You define the roadmap. You'll find the biggest unsolved problems for partners and customers, build conviction around the solution, and ship it. One quarter that might mean defining how partners monetize and measure content through ads; the next, extending platform capabilities to entirely new partner verticals. What stays constant is the expectation you move fast, go deep, and deliver outsized impact.

You are deeply curious, the kind of product leader who digs into partner economics, content supply chains, and ad tech with equal enthusiasm. You're comfortable representing Prime Video directly to senior partner stakeholders and translating their needs into products that scale.

Meet directly with content partners to understand their business models, pain points, and growth ambitions; then translate insights into scalable product strategies.

Speak the language of developers; dive into data, logs, or basic code concepts to unblock your team and accelerate delivery.

Define success metrics, instrument them, and use data to iterate rapidly and make crisp prioritization decisions.

Represent Prime Video externally at partner meetings, industry forums, and executive reviews; positioning us as the most innovative and transparent distributor in streaming.

Leverage AI/ML and emerging technologies to accelerate discovery, prototyping, and delivery.

Influence product and engineering roadmaps without direct authority, building alignment through compelling narratives and data-driven proposals.

descriptionHtml:

title: Systems Development Manager, Region Services
descriptionHtml:
Applicants must be Australian citizens and hold or be eligible to obtain an Australian Government Security Clearance with the ability to successfully complete an Organisational Suitability Assessment. More information regarding security clearances can be found at https://www.agsva.gov.au/.

The Role
As an engineering leader within the AWS Region Services team, you will be the driving force behind operational excellence at massive scale — building the automation, tooling, and systems that keep Australia's most sensitive workloads running flawlessly.

You won't just be maintaining infrastructure. You'll be architecting the operational backbone of a programme that will define how an entire nation defends itself in the digital age. Every tool you build, every process you automate, and every issue you resolve has a direct impact — empowering the analysts, decision-makers, and defenders who depend on this platform every single day.

Key job responsibilities
You'll own the operational heartbeat of one of Australia's most ambitious cloud programmes. Your days will be defined by building — not just fixing — the systems that make massive-scale infrastructure hum.

You'll design and deploy operational tooling that eliminates toil and transforms manual processes into elegant automation. When a repetitive task exists, you'll see it as an engineering problem waiting to be solved. Your code will free your teammates to focus on what matters most: innovation and mission impact.

As a technical leader, you'll hire, develop, and mentor the engineers around you — shaping not just systems, but careers. You'll pair with brilliant colleagues to build and manage services that operate at extraordinary scale, collaborating with some of the leading minds in distributed systems to push the boundaries of what's possible.

When customers face their toughest challenges, you'll be the one who digs deep — diagnosing complex issues across interconnected systems and delivering resolutions that restore confidence. You'll track service health with precision, identifying patterns before they become problems and fixing issues on systems where the margin for error is razor-thin.

You'll participate in a 24/7 on-call rotation, standing as the last line of defence when high-severity issues arise — because in this mission, reliability isn't optional, it's everything.

A day in the life
Your morning starts with a quick scan of service health dashboards — the systems you've built are humming, and the automation you deployed last week has already eliminated three manual runbook steps. You smile. That's engineering with purpose.

By mid-morning, you're deep in code, crafting a new operational tool that will reduce incident response time across the fleet. You're parsing logs with the precision of a surgeon — grep, awk, and sed are second nature — tracing a subtle anomaly through procfs and sysfs until the root cause reveals itself. You push a fix, validate it through your CI/CD pipeline, and watch it roll out seamlessly.

After lunch, you're in a design review with your team, whiteboarding a new approach to service monitoring that leverages systemd hooks and custom metrics. The conversation is electric — ideas bouncing between engineers who genuinely love solving hard problems together. You mentor a newer team member through a tricky networking issue, watching their confidence grow as they master tcpdump and netstat to isolate the fault.

Later, you join a cross-team collaboration session where distributed systems architects are tackling a scaling challenge. Your input on DNS configuration and network topology shapes the solution. Before you wrap up, you review a pull request, leave thoughtful feedback, and update your team's Agile board.

As you close your laptop, you know that the work you did today — the tools you built, the people you coached, the problems you solved — is directly enabling Australia's national security community to operate with speed and confidence they've never had before.

title: Security Engineer II, AWS Vulnerability Management, Third Party Software
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon, Security is our highest priority. Our team builds products and services to continuously identify, track, and mitigate security risks in third-party software and open source libraries across AWS. AWS Security is looking for a Security Engineer to manage security vulnerabilities in third-party software and open source libraries used by AWS applications and services. You'll invent and simplify mechanisms that make updating vulnerable third-party packages a natural part of the software development lifecycle within AWS, and you will have the opportunity to learn from, and be mentored by, those who are building and securing our services.

A Security Engineer at Amazon is expected to be strong in their security domain, for this role it's third party software and open source vulnerability management, and provide contributions to the AWS Security team and to our customers throughout Amazon. Security engineers are expected to develop elegant solutions to complex business problems and apply appropriate technologies while following security engineering best practices. You are also expected to mentor more junior engineers and be a security thought leader for the organization. A Security Engineer must foster constructive dialogue and seek resolution when confronted with discordant views. When solutions fail, they dive deep and make sure that root causes are understood and eliminated with a permanent solution. They take on projects where business and security problems are well understood, but the implementations aren't fully thought out. They balance constraints, limiting the use of short-term workarounds. They ensure the solutions they produce can be maintained and supported or built upon by those not familiar with the space by writing clear documentation and making logical design choices.

You'll be handling complex challenges related to scaling third-party software vulnerability management across AWS's ever-growing infrastructure. This role offers the opportunity to:

descriptionHtml:

You will operate at the intersection of robotics, machine learning, and human-in-the-loop systems, building the infrastructure and methodologies that connect teleoperation, evaluation, and learning. This includes developing evaluation policies, defining task structures, and contributing to operator-facing interfaces that enable scalable and reliable data collection.
The ideal candidate is highly experimental, systems-oriented, and comfortable working across software, robotics, and data pipelines, with a strong focus on turning ambiguous capability goals into measurable and actionable evaluation systems.

Fauna Robotics, an Amazon company, is building capable, safe, and genuinely delightful robots for everyday life. Our goal is simple: make robots people actually want to live and interact with in everyday human spaces.

Our work spans the full stack: mechanical design, control systems, dynamic modeling, and intelligent software. The focus is not just functionality, but experience. We’re building robots that feel responsive, expressive, and genuinely useful.
At Fauna, you’ll work at the frontier of this space, helping define how robots move, manipulate, and interact with people in natural environments. It’s an opportunity to solve hard problems across hardware and software with a team focused on making robotics accessible and joyful to build.

Amazon Web Services' Service Care Center (SCC) is building a new team in Vancouver, and we're looking for a Software Development Manager to lead it. SCC consolidates and automates the operational burden of AWS's 60+ maintenance-mode services, returning builder capacity to innovation. This team owns its efficiency mission. You will lead a group of engineers (Sr. SDE, SDEIIs, SDEIs, and SysDEs) who both operate AWS's most fleet- and compute-heavy maintenance-mode services and build the portfolio-scale automation that detects over-provisioning and tracks footprint reductions across the entire SCC portfolio. Your charter is measurable and ambitious: drive down infrastructure spend, reclaim SDE capacity, and eliminate instances and hosts at scale building each win once and applying it everywhere so operating the Nth service costs a fraction of the first. This is a rare chance to build a brand-new team from the ground up, develop engineers from lever-execution into platform ownership, and make a direct, quantifiable impact on how efficiently AWS runs, all while advancing SCC's NoOps vision of services that run at near-zero builder attention.
We are seeking an experienced software development manager to help us build and lead SCC org in Vancouver to simplify and accelerate the software development experience for 20,000+ AWS engineers. You will shape AWS builder experience from the ground up with a singular mission: make software development, deployment and maintenance simpler across AWS. Success requires building services and tools that reduce friction, listening closely to what your internal customers tell you gets in the way of building, influencing the Amazon Software Builder Experience (ASBX) roadmap, and driving transformation for engineering teams. You will harness advanced technologies, including AI-powered tooling, agentic workflows, and innovative AWS solutions, to create next-generation software builder experience at AWS scale.

This role requires ownership, autonomy, and an ability to deliver results. You should be a self-starter with a bias towards independent problem solving. Clear communication and prioritization will be important as you partner with stakeholders to plan, design, and deliver game changing builder experiences to accelerate innovation. Your passion for improving builder experiences, and proven experience managing complex technology projects, will help you make strong strategic judgments. Roll up your sleeves, build an engineering team second to none, and have fun while creating tons of value to AWS builders!

title: Data Center Controls Tech, Controls Team
descriptionHtml:
As a member of the Global Controls Team, you will collaborate with highly motivated operators, engineers and technicians in the data center industry to maintain and optimize critical infrastructure systems. You will be responsible for troubleshooting and maintaining the Building Management System (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring System (EPMS) while developing new processes and standards that drive innovation in the controls space.

AWS data centers utilize sophisticated industrial control systems to automatically operate mechanical equipment, maintaining optimal temperature and pressure conditions throughout the facilities. These systems integrate and monitor multiple critical components, including generators, uninterruptible power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic and static transfer switches, air-cooled and water-cooled chillers, pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, Computer Room Air Handlers (CRAHs), and air economizers. Within this industrial control system infrastructure, the BMS serves as the primary control platform for all mechanical systems within the data center, while the EPMS functions as the primary monitoring platform for all electrical systems. This position offers the opportunity to work with cutting-edge technology in mission-critical environments while contributing to the reliability and efficiency of AWS's global infrastructure.

Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.

Key job responsibilities
Primarily work in and support multiple data centers by deploying, servicing, and upgrading BMS and EPMS systems.

Mentor and train Facilities team members on the operation and control of BMS and EPMS systems.

Manage small to medium-sized projects and programs.

Perform point-to-point checkouts between field devices and controllers.

Perform first-line diagnostics, troubleshooting, and maintenance of programming code and hardware associated with BMS and EPMS in data centers.

Execute provisioning processes for servers, controllers, industrial PCs, and network configurations, including communication testing between third-party devices and controllers or servers.

Install, replace, configure, and calibrate sensors.

Read and interpret electrical schematics and control panel drawings with a basic understanding of closed-loop controls, field sensor scaling, and functions typically performed by industrial controllers.

Supervise low-voltage electrical contractors performing wiring and installation of field devices in compliance with AWS requirements.

Provide commissioning and systems-level testing support.

Create red-lined drawings and documentation of systems.

Follow change management processes to generate work requests and methods of procedures.

Participate in factory witness tests at vendor or panel builder facilities.

Perform root cause analysis during testing and commissioning.

Ensure personnel on site utilize proper safety methodology.

Perform service activities including monitoring and reviewing ticketing systems, conducting root cause analysis, and prioritizing tasks.

Actively manage service agreements including vendor labor scheduling, quality assurance, and financial invoice review.

Participate in material handling tasks such as lifting, carrying, or moving up to 50 lbs of equipment, and utilize OSHA-standard safety equipment including limited weight-bearing work platforms, ladders, step stools, and personal protective equipment (PPE) such as safety harnesses.

Perform other tasks as assigned by manager.

A day in the life
As a Data Center Controls Technician, your primary customers are Data Center Engineering Operations (DCEO), who rely on you to keep Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring Systems (EPMS) healthy and operational. On a given day, you are the boots on the ground solving problems that directly impact data center availability. You might diagnose a controller communication loss, calibrate instruments feeding inaccurate data to operators, or supervise vendors performing quarterly maintenance. For new builds, you perform point to point testing and support commissioning alongside construction teams. Your internal stakeholders include your Controls Engineer, Controls Manager, partner teams (Field Engineering, Critical Project Implementation, DCEO), and the vendors you oversee.

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Why AWS

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic qualifications

- High school or equivalent diploma
- Associate’s degree, trade school certification, or other certified training in a related technical field with 4+ years of relevant industrial Controls or HVAC controls experience, OR 6+ years of relevant industrial or HVAC controls experience in lieu of a degree.
- Basic understanding of Industrial controls system, knowledge of meters, devices, sensors, relays and troubleshooting utilizing standard hand tools, digital metering, or calibration/diagnostic equipment in a data center, hospitals, large commercial complex, water, power, oil & gas or similar industries.
- 3+ years of experience working with low voltage controls, wiring, networking signals, electrical and mechanical systems, computers and operating systems.
- Ability to work non-standard hours and differing work rotations/shifts and overtime as required.

Preferred qualifications

- Associate's degree in related field
- International Society of Automation (ISA) Certified Controls System Technician (CCST) Level I or higher certification.
- Experience using common communication protocols (MQTT, BACnet, and/or MODBUS).
- 5+ years of experience in controls/automation, construction or related field in a technical environment.
- Demonstrated understanding of engineering documentation, electrical and mechanical diagrams, and standard operating procedures.
- Experience in data centers or mission critical environment
- Fundamental knowledge of network design and layout as well as low voltage (copper/ fiber) cabling.
- Prior AWS/Amazon experience
- 4+ Yr. Military Service

descriptionHtml:
Are you passionate about how SAP workloads transform when they move to the cloud — and about the innovation that becomes possible once they are there? As a Partner Solutions Architect focused on SAP, you will work with AWS Consulting and Technology Partners across EMEA to help them build, migrate, and modernize SAP solutions on AWS, and then unlock new value on top of those estates with AWS data, analytics, generative AI, agentic systems, and intelligent automation.
You will enable partners on SAP on AWS architectures — migration, resilience, security, and modernization — and guide them to combine SAP with AWS capabilities to deliver differentiated customer outcomes at scale. SAP sits at the core of how millions of companies run their day-to-day operations; you will help partners modernize these mission-critical estates and build the next generation of intelligent solutions on top of them, accelerating their customers’ businesses across EMEA.
This is a role for a self-starter who is energised by ambiguity, has a bias for action, and can identify untapped opportunities — someone who sees what others miss and builds where others wait, operating at the intersection of enterprise SAP landscapes, AWS cloud, and emerging technology.

Key job responsibilities
• Support Partner go-to-market motions with technical guidance and thought leadership on SAP on AWS — covering migration, modernization, resilience, security, and innovation on top of SAP.
• Enable AWS Partners and internal AWS teams on the adoption and delivery of SAP on AWS solutions — architecture, migration methodology, workshop delivery, and customer engagement across the full lifecycle.
• Create best practices and architectural guidance on SAP on AWS — landing zones, high availability and disaster recovery, security and compliance, and cost optimization — being a thought leader in the area.
• Drive SAP + AWS innovation — generative AI, agentic AI, and intelligent automation — architecting and delivering demonstrations, proofs of concept, and reference architectures that partners can replicate and customize for their customers.
• Support go-to-market for SAP solutions including SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP), Business Data Cloud, and Cloud ERP (GROW with SAP), tying together AWS and partner offerings across data, analytics, AI, and infrastructure into comprehensive solutions.
• Build and grow partner capabilities (GSIs, ISVs, regional SIs) through enablement workshops, technical guides, and co-build engagements.
• Be the technical reference on SAP for the EMEA Partner Organization, collecting and surfacing the work done across the region.
• Collaborate with AWS account teams, professional services, and commercial sales to bridge partner capabilities with customer demand for SAP transformation.
• Engage line-of-business executives and key stakeholders through business-value-led conversations on strategic opportunities.
• Represent partner needs to AWS service teams, influencing roadmaps and advocating for features that accelerate partner adoption of SAP on AWS.
• Publish thought leadership (blogs, whitepapers, reference architectures), represent AWS at industry events, and contribute to the Partner Solutions Architecture community through knowledge sharing, mentoring, and hiring.


A day in the life
No two days are the same. You might start by whiteboarding an SAP on AWS landing zone with a consulting partner’s delivery team, reviewing high-availability, disaster-recovery, and security design for a large S/4HANA migration. Later, you could be building a generative AI demo on Amazon Bedrock that orchestrates SAP workflows, or showing a partner how to extend SAP with AWS data and analytics services.
After lunch, you might run a workshop with SI partners on a new reference architecture, before ending the day in a strategy session to refine an ongoing sales play based on newly released AWS for SAP solutions. You will also spend time creating reusable enablement assets, guiding partners through SAP on AWS best practices, and collaborating with AWS field teams to match partner capabilities with customer demand. Some days are heavy on building; others on presenting, teaching, or strategizing — but the pace of innovation is constant.

About the team
You will join the EMEA Partner Solutions Architecture (PSA) organization within the AWS Partner Organization (APO). The PSA team serves as a scale engine for AWS, propelling growth by recruiting, activating, and developing partners. We provide the technical enablement and thought leadership that helps partners build and sell solutions on AWS.
This role sits within the Solutions PSA team, which drives AWS growth through differentiated partner solutions across industries and horizontals — including SAP and enterprise applications. The team operates across EMEA, collaborating with commercial sales, industry SAs, and the broader partner ecosystem. You will have flexibility to travel across the region to work directly with partners and attend industry events.
AWS champions diversity and welcomes candidates with non-traditional backgrounds and varied experiences. Our team environment emphasizes curiosity, mentorship, and continuous learning, and we support professional growth while maintaining work-life harmony.

- Experience in specific technology domain areas like software development, cloud computing, systems engineering, infrastructure, security, networking, data and analytics
- Experience communicating across technical and non-technical audiences and at C-level, including training, workshops, publications

- Experience in the automotive and manufacturing domains
- 8+ years of specific technology domain areas (e.g. software development, cloud computing, systems engineering, infrastructure, security, networking, data & analytics) experience
- 3+ years of design, implementation, or consulting in applications and infrastructures experience
- 10+ years of IT development or implementation/consulting in the software or Internet industries experience

- Knowledge of large scale automation and workflow management or equivalent
- Knowledge of database design and implementation or equivalent

You will also play a key role in maintaining our customer expectations to ensure customer orders are delivered at the right time, to the right location.

Our Operation’s workflow has three major components: First mile - where the product is housed and ready for order; Middle mile - where the order is hauled to your area; and Last mile - when the product is delivered to the customer’s door. Please note that all workflows have slight building variations, but one thing is constant: our vision and dedication to the customer.


Our fulfillment network launches new Operations sites every year, providing various opportunities for your professional growth. We hire Area Managers based on location preference and the business’ current openings.

title: Infrastructure Reliability Engineer, Infrastructure Reliability & Quality
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

As an Infrastructure Reliability Engineer you will be proactively driving the reliability risk identification, assessment and mitigation for datacenter infrastructure equipment (Example: PDC and Rack Whips, MC Cables, Busduct, LV SWGR, Breakers, UPS, Power Distribution Cabinets). You will also be responsible for root cause analysis of critical equipment failures, testing and drive the continuous improvements to improve datacenter availability for AWS customers. You will work closely with both internal and outside partners including suppliers to drive key aspects of product specification, risk identification plan, qualification testing and execution. You must be ownership minded, independent, action and results oriented to succeed in an open collaborative environment.

The candidate should have experience in using Physics-of-Failure based approach to develop and implement both analytical and empirical approaches for product quality/reliability risk identification and assessment during product design, manufacture as well as deployment stages. The individual should be able to drive AWS application-specific requirements in carrying out both lifecycle environmental and operational stress driven risk analysis, including thermal, electrical, chemical and mechanical stresses so to identify overstress and fatigue-related product weaknesses. Candidate should be capable of evaluating not only product design quality/reliability risks, but also have the skills and experiences in assessing electronics manufacture process related quality/reliability issues. Knowledge of statistical techniques and models is required to analyze test as well as field data.

At the component level, the individual will drive critical component identification and the associated vendor selection and qualification requirements. The candidate will be expected to use knowledge of process capability for electronic component production as well as system-level performance requirements to establish critical to quality and reliability metrics.

At the system level, the individual will develop datacenter system level reliability model and related reliability quantification and risk analysis for datacenter configuration optimization. The candidate will be expected to be familiar with system reliability engineering tools, such as reliability block diagram, statistical modeling and data analytics.

During sustaining stage, candidate will be responsible for monitoring product performance in the field and will be responsible to drive root cause analysis of any critical failures and the associated corrective and preventive actions. The individual should also be able to drive effective vendor auditing and quarterly review process to drive the continuous improvements of datacenter availability.

The successful candidate should be considered as an expert in the reliability engineering field and have a proven track record of success in not only product reliability leadership, as well as business negotiations and program management. Strong skill-set in problem analysis and solving as well as communication and vendor management are necessary. Candidates should also be able to travel within US and internationally.

title: Software Development Manager, Amazon Simple Storage Service, S3 Express
descriptionHtml:
Managing trillions of objects, retrieving them in sub-millisecond time, deploying software to tens of thousands of hosts, and achieving 99.999999999% durability (yes, that's 11 nines). These numbers hint at the scale of problems you'll tackle every day on Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3). S3 powers businesses across the globe, and we are looking for a Software Development Manager to lead a team building the index layer of S3 Express, our high-performance storage tier. You will own the technical direction for your team's distributed systems, guide engineers through algorithmically complex challenges like noisy-neighbor isolation and sub-millisecond latency, and help shape what could become the largest data storage service on the planet. If you care deeply about growing people, inventing new solutions, and operating at cloud scale, this is the role for you.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the technical vision and roadmap for the S3 Express NameSpace index layer, defining how the system evolves to meet customer latency and durability requirements over the next one to two years.

- Drive solutions to complex performance problems such as noisy-neighbor isolation and sub-millisecond retrieval, partnering closely with front-end and storage system teams to deliver cohesive results.

You might start the morning reviewing latency dashboards and durability metrics for the S3 Express index layer, then join a design review where your engineers walk through a proposal for reducing tail latency. After lunch, you could be working with the front-end systems team to align on an upcoming integration, followed by a one-on-one coaching session with an engineer preparing for their next career step. You'll move between strategic planning and hands-on technical guidance, ensuring your team has the context and support they need to ship high-quality software.

About the team
The S3 Express NameSpace team owns the index layer that underpins Amazon S3 Express, a high-performance storage tier built for workloads that demand single-digit-millisecond access. We sit within the broader Amazon S3 organization and partner closely with front-end and storage system teams to deliver an end-to-end customer experience at massive scale. title: Sr. Specialist Solution Architect - GenAI
descriptionHtml:

Generative AI is moving from experimentation to production, and the customers making that jump need more than a service overview. They need someone who can advise their senior executives on how AI technology can drive their AI journey, sit with their architects, work through what a model can and cannot do for their specific problem, and design something that survives contact with their security review, their data estate and their regulator.

As a Specialist Solutions Architect for AI, you will be the technical voice for your customers for AWS AI services in Germany, Switzerland and CEE, helping customers understand what is genuinely possible with AWS, designing the architectures that get them there, and proving it with them in deep dive engagements. title: Sr. UX Product Researcher, AWS Region Services
descriptionHtml:
As a Senior UX Product Researcher on our team, you'll work alongside engineers, designers, and product managers to bring customer evidence into product and roadmap decisions. You'll go deep on how builders and technical teams actually work, and make sure their needs shape what we build.

You'll lead end-to-end research programs across major product lifecycles, influence strategy through evidence, and help define the experience for the AWS service teams and customers who depend on our products every day.

You'll partner closely with senior leadership and product stakeholders to ensure what we build is grounded in a deep understanding of our users — many of whom are technical builders with sophisticated needs.

Why join us?
- Work closely with engineering and bring customer evidence directly into technical architecture and roadmap decisions.
- Research a sophisticated builder and technical audience whose work powers products used by millions worldwide.
- Shape product and platform strategy through deep user understanding, not just validate decisions after they're made.
- Collaborate with world-class designers, engineers, and product leaders in a culture that values innovation, ownership, and customer obsession.

Key job responsibilities
- Own and manage research programs for major product and service lifecycles, from discovery through launch and post-launch evaluation.
- Design and execute research using a mix of methods suited to a technical audience — including developer and stakeholder interviews, surveys, diary studies, usability testing, and behavioral/log and telemetry analysis.
- Embed with engineering teams to translate customer and builder needs into technical requirements and influence how services are designed.
- Identify new research opportunities that inform product strategy and influence business decisions.
- Translate complex findings into clear, actionable insights for cross-functional partners and senior leadership.
- Inform strategic planning documents (e.g., Press Releases / Working Backwards narratives) with customer evidence and recommendations.
- Navigate ambiguous business problems and define research approaches that drive clarity.
- Contribute to the broader research community through patents, publications, or internal knowledge sharing.

About the team
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

We make it radically easier for AWS service teams and customers to find, understand, and act on the right information about AWS services across regions.

Behind that mission is the Product Registry — the source of truth for AWS service metadata (naming, categorization, lifecycle stage, ownership, hierarchy, regional availability, technical dependencies, and more). Service teams rely on us to track, report, and self-correct their feature catalogs; customers rely on us (through AWS Capabilities by Region and Capability Insights) to understand what's available where. We also help teams achieve parity across AWS regions as they expand.

That's a rich experience problem: our users are technical, their decisions are high-stakes, and their current tools are complex. Research is central to how we decide what to build and judge whether it's working, and you'll have real influence over the direction of the product.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of proven success leading User Research projects with demonstrated impact experience
- 5+ years of hands-on work with: field research, ethnography, lab-based user testing, remote testing, paper prototype testing, iterative prototype testing, concept testing, and survey design experience
- Bachelor's degree in HCDE, Human Factors, Cognitive Psychology, or a related field
- Experience in leading User Research projects with demonstrated impact
- Experience with field research, ethnography, lab-based user testing, remote testing, paper prototype testing, iterative prototype testing, concept testing, and survey design
- Experience with all aspects of research (study design, recruiting, moderation, analysis, reporting)
- Experience with behavioral data collection, quantitative data analysis, and statistics
- Have a portfolio demonstrating past work experience and deliverables (e.g., study plans, reports, personas)

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree in Human Factors, HCDE, Cognitive Psychology or equivalent
- Experience in a technical field (software development, network development, IT, other related)
- Experience with UX Research in non-US markets
- Experience working in a highly Agile/Scrum environment

title: Sr. Partner Sales Manager, FSI
descriptionHtml:
A quota-carrying sales professional responsible for co-sell execution from partner selection through close, driving partner-delivered revenue across assigned territories within Financial Services. The role requires matching partner capabilities to active customer needs, positioning joint value to field and customer stakeholders, and maintaining pipeline discipline across one or more sales territories.

Operating across AWS Marketplace, cloud migrations, and Generative AI, the PSM engages customer, partner, and AWS field stakeholders to build pipeline, increase partner-led deal flow, and deliver revenue against quota.

The ideal candidate operates with minimal direction, prioritizes decisively, escalates with context when deals exceed scope, and builds credibility through consistent execution.

Key job responsibilities
SALES — Revenue Achievement, Co-Sell Execution & Partner Solution Positioning

- Achieve Revenue Targets: Own direct quota accountability across an industry-aligned territory, co-selling with GSI/SIs and ISVs. Prospect, qualify, develop, and close partner-delivered opportunities through joint pursuit plans that align partner capabilities to specific customer outcomes. Maintain pipeline accuracy across AWS and partner CRM systems, advance deals from qualification to close, and deploy co-sell funding mechanisms to compress sales cycles.

- Execute Co-Sell Motions: Co-sell with GSI, SI, and ISV partners to accelerate pipeline and close revenue. Engage partners early in joint accounts to shape deals and establish credibility. Position joint solutions alongside field sellers by connecting partner capabilities to specific customer outcomes. Structure deals to simplify procurement and compress sales cycles.

- Drive Migration-Attached Revenue: Lead cross-functional deal progression for migration opportunities — coordinating GSI/SI delivery partners, positioning solution options (mainframe modernization, DC exit, VMware displacement, app rationalization), and building multi-stakeholder consensus across procurement, IT leadership, and business owners. Accelerate client migration of legacy environments to AWS at scale.


ALLIANCES — Strategic Partner Development & Industry Ecosystem Building

- Develop Strategic Partner Relationships: Build and deepen partner relationships that unlock new line-of-business personas and buying centers within customer accounts. Drive pipeline creation through joint account planning, QBRs, and targeted scale campaigns with the One Partner Team — mapping partner capabilities to high-priority workloads and active customer initiatives to generate qualified co-sell opportunities.

- Shape Partner Co-Sell Deals Through AWS Marketplace: Identify, structure, and advance partner-sourced opportunities that solve customer challenges in areas such as regulatory compliance, data modernization, security, and digital transformation — aligning the right ISV solution to the right business outcome.

- Accelerate Marketplace Adoption: Articulate the financial and operational benefits of consolidated ISV purchasing to procurement, vendor management, and business stakeholders. Position Marketplace as the single platform where clients evaluate and purchase partner solutions — simplifying procurement and reducing cost.

- Own Territory Strategy: Mobilize cross-functional resources across field sales, solution architects, AWS Professional Services, business development, and partner delivery organizations to drive sales velocity. Develop and execute territory plans that map specific partner capabilities to customer transformation priorities — Marketplace adoption, migration programs, and Generative AI readiness — with defined owners, timelines, and success metrics.

- Maintain Operational Discipline: Ensure CRM accuracy, forecast precision, and program utilization tracking. Use AI tools to produce pipeline briefs and risk assessments for leadership. Execute through the OneTeam model, holding cross-functional stakeholders accountable to shared commitments.

- Deliver Against Goals and Mitigate Risk Proactively: Identify blockers early, escalate with context and proposed resolution paths, route field feedback to close execution gaps, and engage the right stakeholders to unblock stalled deals — accelerating close and protecting partner and customer trust.

Key job responsibilities

- Installing Fiber and Copper cabling and patching cabling between equipment

title: Sr. Product Manager, Progression Intelligence
descriptionHtml:
As a Senior Product Manager on the Lifecycle Experiences team, you will own the product vision and execution roadmap for our Progression Intelligence charter. This charter sits at the intersection of machine learning, real-time decisioning, and customer lifecycle strategy - and is responsible for determining which customers to engage, with what action, at what moment, and through which channel.

You will lead the technical integration of our rewards optimization, causal measurement, and action intelligence systems onto a unified agentic orchestration platform - enabling faster experimentation, more personalized interventions, and greater operational efficiency across all our emerging locales.

This is a deeply technical role that requires equal comfort with ML systems, API architecture, and product strategy. You will work closely with applied scientists, software engineers, and marketing stakeholders to ship systems that directly delight millions of customers.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the multi-year product roadmap for Progression Intelligence, including the phased migration of core ML models and decisioning systems onto a unified orchestration platform
- Define technical requirements and integration specifications for connecting rewards optimization, propensity modeling, causal incrementality measurement, and promotion configuration systems into a cohesive, real-time decisioning layer
- Partner with applied scientists to translate model outputs into actionable product features - including reward denomination optimization, next-best-action recommendations, and personalized campaign triggers
- Drive quarterly planning and prioritization across a portfolio of integrations, balancing technical debt, engineering capacity, and business impact
- Define and own success metrics for the Progression Intelligence platform - including model coverage, decisioning latency, incremental lift, and customer settlement outcomes
- Write product requirement documents and participate in technical design reviews, and lead alignment across engineering, science, and business stakeholders
- Represent the Progression Intelligence charter in senior leadership reviews, including weekly business reviews and annual planning cycles
- Identify and resolve technical dependencies and cross-team blockers to keep the integration roadmap on track

About the team
The Lifecycle Experiences team is on a mission to deepen customer engagement across Amazon's fastest-growing marketplaces. title: Applied Scientist II, Amazon Business - External Integrations
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Business System Integrations connects Amazon Business with millions of business users and thousands of partner procurement, ERP, and finance systems. We build the APIs, protocols, and agentic experiences that let customers buy on Amazon Business directly from the systems they already use. As an Applied Scientist on this team, you will own and advance the ML and GenAI capabilities that make these integrations smarter, faster, and more reliable. You will drive model accuracy, scientific innovation, and global scale across external systems integrations.

Our work includes API-based and protocol-based shopping, such as punchout and emerging agent protocols, along with agentic interactions where buyers and AI agents search, compare, and purchase through natural language. It also covers partner onboarding and integration automation, mapping and normalizing catalog, product, and order data across many partner formats, and evaluation frameworks that measure the quality, accuracy, and latency of our agents.
Key job responsibilities
As an Applied Scientist on this team, you will work across three dimensions: Invent, Implement, and Influence.

Invent: You bring deep domain knowledge and fluency with state-of-the-art scientific approaches and emerging research. You practice customer-obsessed science, working backwards from the needs of business buyers, procurement teams, and integration partners to extend or invent new ML approaches, even when no textbook solution exists. You design novel ML and LLM-based methods for agentic shopping, product search and matching, schema and data mapping across partner systems, and automated evaluation of agent quality. You help define the research agenda for our agentic and protocol-based capabilities, and you lead the scientific strategy for accurate, low-latency responses in conversational and API-driven procurement. You author or co-author articles for internal or external peer-reviewed venues when appropriate and not precluded by business considerations.

Implement: The ML components you develop are integrated directly into production systems serving Amazon Business customers and partners worldwide. You make sound tradeoffs between accuracy and latency, innovation and stability, and short-term and long-term solutions, favoring reuse and established frameworks where appropriate. You make progress semi-autonomously with only occasional guidance, implement at the right level of complexity the first time, and evaluate emerging technologies, including LLMs and GenAI frameworks, largely on your own. You ensure your models and pipelines integrate robustly with catalog, offer, cart, order, and partner data sources and with the services that power external integrations.

Influence: You contribute to planning for the team, including goals, priorities, and roadmaps for ML and GenAI capabilities. You lead the scientific strategy for expanding agentic and integration capabilities across new partners, protocols, and countries. You collaborate with engineering, product, and program teams across Amazon Business so that data integration and ML pipelines are robust and scale with adoption. You mentor scientists and engineers, champion best practices for the AI-Driven Development Life Cycle (AIDLC), and provide peer feedback on research methods and results. You help recruit bar-raising talent through interview drives, and you are visible in the broader scientific community as a subject matter expert, including serving as a Program Committee member or reviewer for peer-reviewed venues.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of building models for business application experience
- Experience in patents or publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals
- Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
- Experience in any of the following areas: algorithms and data structures, parsing, numerical optimization, data mining, parallel and distributed computing, high-performance computing
- Master's degree, or PhD

Preferred qualifications

- Experience using Unix/Linux
- Experience in professional software development

descriptionHtml:

title: Senior Supply Chain Manager, Technology Supply Chain Organization Program Enablement
descriptionHtml:

You will design and own the model that quantifies the value Tech-SC delivers that a third party can't match: uptime, readiness, and capital efficiency. You will turn "what is this worth to Amazon" into a defensible number leadership and partner business units rely on to make sourcing and investment decisions.

Key job responsibilities

You work closely with finance partners to align baselines, with supply chain planners on capacity and positioning, and with your leadership to shape strategy.
